title: FreshnessResult::Fresh carries no presence level while Stale does, forcing a re-enumerate
description:
persona-attestors/src/lib.rs:76-85. `Stale(PresenceLevel)` reports the decayed level, `Fresh` reports nothing. A caller polling `freshness()` to keep a live view of presence (which is what lib.rs:132-134 says the method is for) gets the current level only on the stale path; on the fresh path it must call `enumerate()` again and re-match the claim to learn whether presence is still Hardware or has dropped to Session while remaining "fresh". Neither the trait nor `Claim` says whether the level in the caller original `Claim` is still authoritative after a `Fresh` result.

The contract is also unstated in the other direction: it is not documented whether `Stale(level)` must be less than the claim original presence, whether `Stale(Hardware)` is meaningful, or whether the caller should mutate its stored `Claim` with the returned level. persona-attestors/src/oidc.rs:196-201 returns `Stale(PresenceLevel::None)` for a claim whose presence was already `None` (oidc.rs:86), i.e. stale-with-no-change, while ssh.rs:151-157 never returns Stale at all.

Making both arms carry the level — `Fresh(PresenceLevel)` / `Stale(PresenceLevel)`, or a single `{ fresh: bool, presence: PresenceLevel }` — removes the asymmetry and the extra round trip. Free now; the enum is non_exhaustive but changing an existing variant payload is not.
